tasks.title: Create an HTML5 Boilerplate Document
tasks.description: Create a complete HTML5 boilerplate document with the correct doctype declaration, html, head, and body elements. Include a title in the head section.
tasks.hint: Remember that HTML5 uses `<!DOCTYPE html>` at the very top of the document. The `<html>` tag should have a `lang` attribute.

tasks.title: Build a Table with Semantic Elements
tasks.description: Build a table with `thead`, `tbody`, and `tfoot` sections using proper semantic HTML elements. Include at least 3 rows of data.
tasks.hint: Use `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>` elements. Headers go in `<th>` tags.

tasks.title: Create a Navigation Section Using Semantic HTML
tasks.description: Create a complete page layout using semantic HTML elements including `<nav>`, `<header>`, `<section>`, and `<footer>`. The navigation should contain at least 3 links.
tasks.hint: Semantic HTML helps with accessibility and SEO. Use `<nav>` for navigation, `<header>` for the top of the page, `<section>` for content areas, and `<footer>` for the bottom.

tasks.title: Build a Page with Heading Hierarchy and Nested Lists
tasks.description: Build a page that demonstrates proper heading hierarchy from `<h1>` to `<h6>` and includes nested ordered and unordered lists with at least 3 levels of nesting.
tasks.hint: Headings should be used in order without skipping levels. Lists can be nested by placing a new `<ul>` or `<ol>` inside an `<li>` element.

tasks.title: Create a Registration Form
tasks.description: Create a registration form with username, email, and password fields. Each field should have a corresponding `<label>` element.
tasks.hint: Use `<form>`, `<input>`, and `<label>` elements. The `for` attribute on labels should match the `id` on inputs.

tasks.title: Build a Form with Various Input Types
tasks.description: Build a form that includes radio buttons, checkboxes, and a select dropdown menu. Group related inputs using `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`.
tasks.hint: Radio buttons share the same `name` attribute. Checkboxes can have individual `name` attributes. Use `<select>` with `<option>` elements for dropdowns.

tasks.title: Create a Form with Advanced Input Types
tasks.description: Create a form with file input, date input, and color input fields. Add appropriate labels and basic validation attributes.
tasks.hint: Use `type="file"`, `type="date"`, and `type="color"`. You can add `required`, `min`, `max`, and `accept` attributes for validation.

tasks.title: Style a Page Using All Three CSS Methods
tasks.description: Style a page using all three CSS methods: inline styles, an internal `<style>` block, and an external CSS file linked via `<link>`.
tasks.hint: Inline styles go in the `style` attribute. Internal CSS goes in a `<style>` tag in the `<head>`. External CSS uses a `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">` tag.

tasks.title: Apply Styles Using Different Selectors
tasks.description: Apply styles to elements using element selectors, class selectors, and ID selectors. Create at least one example of each.
tasks.hint: Element selectors target HTML tags directly (e.g., `p`). Class selectors use a dot prefix (e.g., `.classname`). ID selectors use a hash prefix (e.g., `#idname`).

tasks.title: Create a Box Model Layout
tasks.description: Create a layout that demonstrates proper use of margin, padding, and border using the CSS box model. Include elements with different box-sizing values.
tasks.hint: Use `box-sizing: border-box` to include padding and border in the element's total width. Use `margin` for space outside the border and `padding` for space inside.

tasks.title: Position Elements Using Different Positioning Methods
tasks.description: Position elements on a page using relative, absolute, and fixed positioning. Demonstrate how each positioning method affects document flow.
tasks.hint: Relative positioning keeps the element in the document flow. Absolute positioning removes it from flow and positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor. Fixed positioning is relative to the viewport.

tasks.title: Build a Layered Layout Using Z-Index
tasks.description: Build a layered layout using `z-index` and positioning to stack multiple elements on top of each other with proper layering control.
tasks.hint: `z-index` only works on positioned elements (position relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky). Higher z-index values appear on top of lower values.

tasks.title: Center a Div Using Flexbox
tasks.description: Center a div both horizontally and vertically on the page using CSS Flexbox properties.
tasks.hint: Set `display: flex` on the parent container. Use `justify-content: center` for horizontal centering and `align-items: center` for vertical centering.

tasks.title: Create a Navigation Bar Using Flexbox
tasks.description: Create a responsive navigation bar using Flexbox with `justify-content` and `align-items` properties to distribute and align navigation items.
tasks.hint: Use `display: flex` on the nav container. `justify-content: space-between` or `space-around` can spread items evenly. `align-items: center` vertically centers them.

tasks.title: Build a Card Layout Using Flex-Wrap and Flex-Grow
tasks.description: Build a card layout that uses `flex-wrap` to wrap cards to the next line and `flex-grow` to make cards expand to fill available space.
tasks.hint: Use `flex-wrap: wrap` on the container. Set `flex-grow: 1` on cards to make them expand. Use `flex-basis` to set the initial size before growing.

tasks.title: Create a Responsive Grid Layout Using Flexbox
tasks.description: Create a responsive grid layout using Flexbox properties that adapts to different screen sizes without using CSS Grid or media queries.
tasks.hint: Combine `flex-wrap: wrap` with `flex-basis` and `flex-grow` to create a fluid grid. Use percentage-based widths or calc() for responsiveness.

tasks.title: Define and Use CSS Custom Properties
tasks.description: Define CSS custom properties (variables) in the `:root` selector and use them throughout your stylesheet to maintain consistent theming.
tasks.hint: Define variables with `--variable-name: value;` in `:root`. Access them with `var(--variable-name)`. You can provide fallback values with `var(--variable-name, fallback)`.

tasks.title: Create a Hover Transition Effect
tasks.description: Create smooth hover transition effects using CSS pseudo-classes and the `transition` property. Include at least two different property transitions.
tasks.hint: Use `:hover` pseudo-class to define the hover state. Use `transition` property to animate changes (e.g., `transition: all 0.3s ease`).

tasks.title: Build a Keyframe Animation for a Loading Spinner
tasks.description: Build a loading spinner animation using CSS `@keyframes` and the `animation` property.
tasks.hint: Define `@keyframes` with `from` and `to` (or percentage-based) steps. Use `animation` shorthand to apply it (e.g., `animation: spin 1s linear infinite`).

tasks.title: Create a Responsive Layout Using CSS Grid and Media Queries
tasks.description: Create a responsive layout using CSS Grid combined with media queries that adapts the grid structure for mobile, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.
tasks.hint: Use `display: grid` with `grid-template-columns`. Use `@media` queries to change the grid layout at different breakpoints (e.g., `@media (max-width: 768px)`).
